question: Are fiber gap candidates over-represented in fallback-interpolated control-point spans compared with native trace spans?

inputs.byte_rule: every fiber is re-downloaded and must match its census SHA-256; any download or hash failure makes the run RUN FAILED, never a smaller sample

definitions.span: control point k to control point k+1; line range [nearest line index of k, nearest line index of k+1)
definitions.gap_step: line step longer than gap_factor x the fiber's median non-zero line step (scroliq-fiber rule)
definitions.gap_positive_span: span containing at least one gap step
definitions.non_monotone_fiber: nearest control indices decrease; excluded from the test and listed by name

decision.statistic: pooled span-level risk difference P(gap | fallback) - P(gap | native)
decision.ci: 95% percentile interval from a fiber-cluster bootstrap
decision.secondary: Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio stratified by fiber (fibers with both span types)
decision.rule: SUPPORTED iff the CI lower bound > 0 AND the MH odds ratio > 1; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED
decision.insufficient: INSUFFICIENT if fewer informative fibers or fallback spans than the minimums

controls.positive: on the real span structure, plant gap outcomes only in fallback spans at positive_fallback_rate; the decision must return SUPPORTED
controls.null: on the real span structure, draw gap outcomes independent of mode at the observed overall rate; the decision must return SUPPORTED in no more than max_null_false_positive_rate of null_replicates
controls.failure: If either control fails the verdict is CONTROL FAILURE and no scientific claim is made

descriptive_only: mechanism: per-span median step / fiber median step, fallback vs native (tests the sparser-rendering hypothesis; not part of the decision)
gap steps outside every span (before the first or after the last control)
VC3D PointCollections export of every gap candidate (goal O10)
interpretation_limits: SUPPORTED is an association at span level, not proof that fallback interpolation causes trace breaks: gap steps are defined relative to rendered step length, so sparser fallback rendering alone could produce it (see the mechanism arm).
No CT is read; nothing here says whether a gap is a physical sheet break.
